research_scope: Source-free independent Wave2 contextual prerequisite review, five fully source-inspected alias identities; no new meanings, no original text edits, no external research, certification, or consolidation.

aliases.reason: The categorical fibre-product and scheme fibre-product sources each have maps X→S and Y→S and a vertex T or P with maps u:T→X, v:T→Y satisfying fu=gv, i.e. a cone over the cospan-shaped diagram. The generic category-limit source defines a cone on F:I→C by arrows L→F(i) compatible with diagram arrows, with no universality required. Taking I to be the cospan indexing category gives precisely the same underlying cone prerequisite. Pullback universality and the scheme-specific category remain distinct parent conditions; this does not equate arbitrary cones with pullback limits.

The essentially-constant ind-diagram parent invokes maps M_i→X compatible with all transitions of a filtered diagram, without asserting X is the colimit. The generic category-colimit parent defines exactly this compatible family as a cocone F(i)→Q, with I arbitrary and the colimit universal property added separately. The first is an instance using I filtered, F(i)=M_i and Q=X. This is an identity of the underlying cocone prerequisite only, not an identity of filteredness, essential constancy and colimit universality.

The Tor flatness local-criterion source takes a local homomorphism R→S of Noetherian local rings; the locally ringed space and scheme morphism sources require homomorphisms between local stalk rings that are local. In both cases the foundational condition is f^{-1}(m_S)=m_R for the respective maximal ideals. The stronger Noetherian, stalkwise, morphism-of-sheaves and Tor hypotheses remain in their parent texts. Equivalently requiring f(m_R)⊆m_S is valid for unital maps of local rings.

The left R-module kernel parent writes ker(φ)=φ^{-1}({0_N}), explicitly a set-theoretic preimage of the singleton zero under the underlying function φ:M→N, with no invertibility requirement. The existing broadly recurring inverse-image prerequisite defines f^{-1}[B]={x:f(x)∈B} for every function and subset of the codomain. Taking f=φ and B={0_N} identifies the prerequisite exactly; R-linearity, the submodule property and the kernel equation stay parent-specific.

For directed R-module transitions u_ij:M_i→M_j, the source's reverse Hom transition Hom_R(M_j,N)→Hom_R(M_i,N) sends f to f∘u_ij, hence uses exactly the categorical precomposition operation already recorded from representable presheaves and functors of points. Module-linearity and preservation of identity/composition are respected, while direction-indexed system coherence and eventual-image stabilization defining the Mittag-Leffler condition remain parent-specific; the entire Hom inverse system is not identified with an arbitrary representable presheaf.
